warnings.warning: The unlimited exponential baseline is introduced without observed growth data, time units, or a check that a single undivided state is appropriate.
The logistic equation changes r' and K' notation when later stage equations use r and K, but the relationship between the parameters is not defined.
The juvenile differential equation mixes a female-driven birth term and maturation outflow without units, initial conditions, or a derivation of r.
The adult equations impose one mortality rate on females and males despite later arguments that sex-specific energy and resistance differ.
Eq.1 assumes every matured juvenile enters a binary female/male flow and does not state timing or loss during differentiation.
Eq.2 treats rF(1-B/K) as a monthly count while r is called a growth rate; stock-flow units and positivity conditions are unreported.
Eq.3 requires a female maturation history and nonnegative update rule, neither of which is specified.
Eq.4 likewise lacks the initial delay history and a clipping or feasibility rule for negative male abundance.
Eq.5 sums cohort birth terms but does not define whether overlapping or state-dependent delays can assign one cohort to multiple maturation months.
Eq.6 uses alpha_i indexed by birth month although prose defines alpha_t in the month of sex differentiation; the timing convention is ambiguous.
Eq.7 inherits the same alpha-index ambiguity and gives no condition enforcing alpha in [0,1].
The text cites Assumption 5 for the alpha-tau relation, but only Assumptions 1-4 are numbered; the fitted c/d data and protocol are absent.
The energy-threshold derivation alternates food/B minus waste with eta*food/B without defining waste, units, assimilation bookkeeping, or cohort-specific abundance.
The reported k=-0.000844 makes tau decrease as B increases, conflicting with the preceding bound tau proportional to B and the later per-capita-energy feedback narrative.
Eq.8 uses epsilon_F as a predation-loss coefficient while prose calls larger epsilon easier to be predated; the sign is plausible but values, units, and evidence are absent.
Eq.9 supplies a separate epsilon_M without data supporting sex-specific predation or checking identifiability against mortality.
Eq.10 prints mu_P but the definition bullet says mu_t, and theta is described as lamprey unit energy rather than a predator conversion coefficient.
Eq.11 applies Nicholson-Bailey escape to one host but omits host density dependence, lamprey survival, other hosts, parameter units, and calibration.
Eq.12 generates parasites from attacked adult lampreys but omits parasite survival, fecundity/conversion, density dependence, and any direct feedback on F and M in the displayed equation.
The prose defines Simpson's index as the probability of selecting two members of the same species, but Eq.13 is one minus that concentration.
Eq.14 does not state zero-share handling, species inclusion rules, sampling window, or whether base-two units matter to comparisons.
Eq.15 claims seasonal mortality but prints sin(2*pi/T) without time t, making the A1 term constant; the dangling t0 definition crosses the page.
Eq.16 assumes random mixing and equal mating capacity so a product of sex shares measures genetic transmission; age, fecundity, pairing, and density are omitted.

The feedback explanation first says a disturbance in B increases per-capita nutrition and later calls it an initial decrease; Figure 13 is cited where Figure 12 is intended, and loop gain is not computed.
Eq.17 calls a larger maximum deviation resistance stability even though the paper interprets smaller values as more stable; it is a loss metric unless transformed.
Eq.18 does not define t1, t2, a recovery tolerance, or how recovery is detected for oscillatory or noisy curves.
Eq.19 is continuous while the simulation is monthly discrete; no quadrature, normalization, unit handling, or horizon comparability is specified.
The fixed and adaptive panels use visibly different horizons in some figures, yet extinction, persistence, and stability are compared without matched windows.
Table 2 averages G over an unstated window and supplies no raw series, transient rule, uncertainty, or independent demographic validation.
Figures 14b and 15b plot the time-varying absolute gap, not the scalar integrated S, and remain nonzero after the second disturbance despite an unconditional recovery claim.
The diversity workflow omits the species set, abundance denominator, extinction rule, time window, raw series, and uncertainty, so Hmean and Dmean cannot be reproduced.
Three selected values per parameter and visual curve inspection do not establish model stability, normalized sensitivity, uncertainty robustness, or structural robustness.

global_organization_chain: A Great Lakes control context and the unusual resource-responsive sex ratio motivate a population-and-ecosystem study.
The paper compresses the life cycle into juvenile, adult female, and adult male states and converts a logistic differential model into a one-month delayed difference system.
Development time tau determines the maturation cohort, alpha splits that cohort by sex, and fitted or asserted alpha-tau and tau-B relations close the BFM model.
Sex-separated Lotka-Volterra and Nicholson-Bailey modules connect lampreys to a predator, host, and parasite before Simpson and Shannon indices summarize community diversity.
Suitable and mortality-perturbed scenarios compare fixed and variable alpha, after which breeding success exposes a stability-versus-reproduction tradeoff.
A qualitative feedback schematic and phase trajectories interpret growing oscillations as positive feedback and bounded cycles as negative feedback.
Maximum deviation, recovery duration, integrated deviation, and biodiversity means translate the population experiments into an ecosystem-stability answer.

Selected rH, K, and mortality cases lead to invasion-control suggestions, followed by strengths, a semi-quantitative limitation, references, and a disclosed AI-use appendix excluded from team-language evidence.

main_argument_chains.claim: A stage- and sex-structured delayed BFM can represent lamprey population dynamics.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the cohort-delay architecture, but require a defined update order, complete initial history, parameter units, positivity rules, and executable parity.
support_steps: start from exponential and logistic growth

main_argument_chains.claim: Resource-dependent alpha and tau improve coexistence with predators, hosts, and parasites relative to constant values.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain the paired module comparison while treating coexistence and extinction as conditional simulations until data, parameter provenance, horizon matching, uncertainty, and independent validation are supplied.
support_steps: compare fixed and variable alpha trajectories

main_argument_chains.claim: Variable sex ratios improve biodiversity in the larger ecosystem.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Preserve the indicator-to-task chain, but resolve the Simpson definition conflict, species set, averaging window, extinction threshold, uncertainty, and causal attribution.

main_argument_chains.claim: Variable alpha stabilizes the lamprey population but lowers breeding success.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report an explicit stability-versus-mating-opportunity tradeoff; do not infer long-term evolution or living-fossil status from one internal proxy without genetic or demographic validation.

main_argument_chains.claim: A new negative-feedback loop explains the improved stability.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the sign-loop explanation as a hypothesis, while requiring corrected cross-references, clarified alpha settings, Jacobian or loop-gain analysis, equilibrium conditions, and parameter-regime checks before assigning feedback type.
support_steps: map nutrition to tau and alpha
inspect schematic and F-B-t phase trajectories

main_argument_chains.claim: Variable alpha improves resistance, resilience, comprehensive stability, and biodiversity.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain the metric sequence but rename loss-direction indicators, define t1/t2 and recovery tolerance, report the scalar area, correct Table 3/4, and propagate simulation uncertainty.
support_steps: define S1 as maximum curve gap

main_argument_chains.claim: Sensitivity results support practical lamprey-control guidance.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Classify this as selected-case numerical exploration, not broad robustness; require ranges, normalized sensitivity, matched controls, multi-parameter interactions, correct intervention-to-parameter mapping, and empirical calibration.
support_steps: recommend host protection and dual-stage control
